title: Dispatch CSA 8: Miss Quill Returns Alone Through East Quay Door
summary: The Calder aperture closed as the final member of the survey reached Alderwick.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Ada Quill emerged at 8:04 last evening from a locked storeroom at the Mariners’ Rest. She was soaked, barefoot, and carrying the central spindle of the Calder ranging anchor. Three minutes earlier, Professor Vey, Mr. Rook, and Miss Bell had come through the Institute aperture. Their receiver ceased sounding as Miss Quill crossed the threshold on East Quay.

The account assembled from the party’s messages describes a difficult separation at the black stone. Miss Quill released the spindle while the others followed the clear tone toward the Institute. The many reflected paths collapsed into a single passage, but the water rose between her and her companions. She followed a faint second tone toward the storeroom whose door Alderwick residents had seen open days before.

She had carried the receiver’s small sounding coil in her pocket. “Mara made two,” she told our reporter, referring to the younger Miss Bell. “One for the people running home. One for whoever had to stay.” Miss Bell confirmed the detail and said she had not told the returnees about the second coil.

As the aperture closed, the three returnees in the Institute’s west wing vanished from their beds. An attendant standing beside the returned Professor Vey reported no light, sound, or disturbance. His blanket fell flat. Their belongings remain, including the six pages from Mr. Rook’s log and the receiver made by the returned Miss Bell.

Miss Quill has declined to call the returnees mistaken or unreal. “They brought us the warning,” she said. “Mara built the way back. I wish they had lived to see it work.” Dr. Marr has ordered all surviving apparatus sealed pending an inquiry.
